docs.title: Keeping and discarding taxa
docs.text:
Every amplicon run ends with a set of ASVs, each carrying a taxonomy string. Some of those ASVs are not what the study is about: chloroplast and mitochondrial reads co-amplified by 16S primers, plant or host sequences in an ITS run, a Ralstonia that came in with the extraction kit, a parE paralog picked up by gyrB primers. The taxonomy filter is where they are removed.

It is a plain keep/discard list of taxon names, set in amplicon.taxonomy.filter. The keep and discard lists have no built-in default and no per-marker rules in the code: what the config lists is exactly what is applied. For 16S there is one more step that is not a list: ASVs that Metaxa2 calls mitochondria or chloroplast are removed too (the organelle filter, on by default).

docs.title: Where the filter sits in the run
docs.text:
The filter is the last thing that happens inside the assign_taxonomy rule, after classification and before any table is written.

Step What happens Input 05.dada2/seqs_lenfilt.fasta (ASV sequences after the length filter, and after Metaxa2/ITSx extraction where that runs) plus the matching count table 05.dada2/seqtab_lenfilt_head_names.txt Classify rdp path — DADA2 assignTaxonomy (+ addSpecies for 16S); sintax path — vsearch --sintax Build lineage ranks joined into one taxonomy string per ASV Filter keep, then discard, applied to that string; then discard's best-hit check; for 16S, then Metaxa2's organelle call Output 06.taxonomy/asv_table.txt, asv_table_seqs.txt, taxon_seq_table.txt (filtered), and asv_table_unfiltered.txt (every ASV, with what the filter did to it)

The two classifier paths are separate scripts — workflow/scripts/amplicon/80a_assign_taxonomy.R for rdp and workflow/scripts/amplicon/80c_parse_sintax.py for sintax — but they implement the same filter with the same behaviour, so the choice of classifier does not change how the lists are written.

The filter removes whole ASVs. A discarded ASV disappears from all three output tables at once, counts included, and nothing downstream re-adds it. The one file that still lists it is asv_table_unfiltered.txt, which exists for exactly that. The cost in reads is visible in stats/read_tracking.txt, whose post_taxonomy_filter column is summed from the filtered asv_table.txt: comparing it with post_length_filter shows how many reads the filter removed, per sample.

Note

Read classification itself is untouched. The filter only decides which of the classified ASVs are written out; it never changes the taxonomy an ASV was given.

docs.title: How matching works
docs.text:
Each ASV's taxonomy string is a lineage with ranks joined by ; (no space), each rank carrying its own prefix. Which ranks a string has follows the marker's reference: a 16S string on SILVA 144, for example, reads

d__…;k__…;p__…;c__…;o__…;f__…;g__…;s__…

while on SILVA 138.2 it has no k__ slot and on ITS no d__ slot. The slots of every marker are listed under taxonomy strings in the final tables.

A token in keep or discard is compared against whole rank segments of that string — the pieces between the semicolons — not against the string as a whole. A token matches when it is exactly equal to one of those segments.

That is what makes the lists safe to use at any rank. g__Bacillus matches an ASV whose genus is exactly Bacillus, and nothing else: not a differently suffixed genus such as g__Bacillus_A, and not a species or family segment that happens to contain the same letters.

One exception is deliberate. SILVA 144 marks some clades X--other (a clade that does not contain the type of taxon X but is still considered part of it), and the filter ignores that suffix on both sides: g__Bradyrhizobium also matches g__Bradyrhizobium--other. Labels that SILVA 144 merges with + (g__Enterobacter--other+Klebsiella--other) are not split; to match one, use the whole label as the token. See 16S rRNA.

An ASV passes the filter as follows:

  • keep runs first and defines what survives. An ASV is kept only if at least one of its ranks matches a keep token. keep: [d__Bacteria, d__Archaea] therefore keeps prokaryotes and drops both eukaryotic hits and anything left unclassified at domain level — an ASV with an empty lineage matches nothing, so it does not survive a non-empty keep.
  • discard then prunes what remains. An ASV is removed if any of its ranks matches a discard token. discard: [o__Chloroplast, f__Mitochondria] removes the usual 16S plastid and host carry-over.
  • discard also checks the best hit (discard_min_support, below): an ASV is removed when the classifier's best hit carries a discard token at that token's rank with enough support, even if that rank fell below the confidence cutoff and is missing from the reported lineage.
  • For 16S, Metaxa2's organelle call comes last (organelles, below): an ASV that Metaxa2 called mitochondria or chloroplast is removed even when no token matched it.
  • Because discard runs second, it wins: a taxon named in both lists is removed.

docs.title: The five keys
docs.text:
amplicon:
  taxonomy:
    filter:
      enabled: true
      keep:    [d__Bacteria, d__Archaea]
      discard: [o__Chloroplast, f__Mitochondria]
      discard_min_support: 50
      organelles: metaxa2
Key Effect enabled Master switch. false turns the filter off entirely and every classified ASV is written out, whatever keep and discard contain. keep Tokens that define what survives. An empty list (or the key left unset) means this direction does nothing — no ASV is dropped for failing to match. discard Tokens that are then removed from the survivors. An empty list means this direction does nothing. discard_min_support Best-hit check for discard, in percent (0–100). Default 50; null switches it off. See below. organelles 16S only: metaxa2 (default) also removes the ASVs Metaxa2 calls mitochondria or chloroplast; off does not. Does nothing for the other markers. See below.

Both lists accept a bare scalar as well as a YAML list, so keep: k__Fungi and keep: [k__Fungi] are equivalent.

Two consequences worth spelling out, because they are easy to conflate:

  • enabled: true with both lists empty is a working filter that removes nothing, except on 16S, where the organelle filter still removes the ASVs Metaxa2 calls mitochondria or chloroplast (organelles: off stops that too). That is the fail-safe state, not an error.
  • enabled: false with populated lists ignores those lists completely, and switches the organelle filter off as well. It is the quick way to test what the filter was actually costing. The tokens are still checked when the run starts, so that they are right on the run that switches the filter back on (see when MetaFlux refuses a token at start-up).

docs.title: Why the shipped config has the values commented out
docs.text:
config/config.yaml is always loaded as a base layer underneath the --configfile given on the command line. Any concrete value written there would silently apply to every run that does not override it — 16S tokens leaking into an 18S run, for instance, where keep: [d__Bacteria, d__Archaea] would discard every eukaryotic ASV. So the template ships the recommended values commented out:

      keep:    #[d__Bacteria, d__Archaea]
      discard: #[o__Chloroplast, f__Mitochondria]

Left unset they resolve to [], which filters nothing. Copy the line for the marker in use into the run config and uncomment it there. discard_min_support and organelles ship set. The first does nothing until discard lists a token; the second acts only on 16S with extraction on, and does nothing for any other marker.

docs.title: The best-hit check (discard_min_support)
docs.text:
The taxonomy each ASV is reported with stops at the last rank whose confidence reaches min_boot (rdp) or sintax_cutoff (sintax). Below that rank the classifier still has a best guess; it is simply not confident enough to report it. For most taxa that is the right behaviour. For organelle 16S it lets contaminants through: a mitochondrial ASV whose best hit is Mitochondria at 60% support is reported as p__Pseudomonadota, so f__Mitochondria never sees it. Plant and algal mitochondria are diverse, SILVA 144 holds many of them, and the classifiers often stay below 80% at order and family level for them.

So, for every ASV that survived keep and discard, each discard token is also compared with the best hit's name at the token's own rank (o__ = Order, f__ = Family, and so on), and the ASV is removed when the names match and the support at that rank is at least discard_min_support:

Method Support used rdp the bootstrap support of that rank (0–100), from DADA2 assignTaxonomy sintax the confidence of that rank in the full best-hit lineage VSEARCH reports (0–1, compared ×100)

The keep list is not affected, and s__ tokens are only ever compared with the reported lineage (the species from addSpecies has no support value). Each ASV removed this way gets its own log line, as here on the 16S test set (PRJNA305879) under method: rdp with SILVA 144:

[assign_taxonomy]   ASV_104: best hit f__Mitochondria at 60% support (reported as d__Bacteria;k__Pseudomonadati;p__Pseudomonadota)
[assign_taxonomy]   ASV_19: best hit f__Mitochondria at 70% support (reported as d__Bacteria;k__Pseudomonadati;p__Pseudomonadota;c__Alphaproteobacteria)
[assign_taxonomy]   ASV_198: best hit f__Mitochondria at 54% support (reported as d__Bacteria;k__Pseudomonadati;p__Pseudomonadota;c__Alphaproteobacteria)
[assign_taxonomy]   ASV_25: best hit f__Mitochondria at 62% support (reported as d__Bacteria;k__Pseudomonadati;p__Pseudomonadota)
[assign_taxonomy] Discard filter, best-hit check (support >= 50%): 4 more ASV(s) removed

The default of 50 means the best hit needs at least half the support at that rank (50 of 100 bootstrap draws, or a SINTAX confidence of 0.5). Set it higher to be more conservative, or to null to get the filter of MetaFlux v2.4.0 and earlier.

docs.title: The organelle filter (organelles)
docs.text:
For 16S, Metaxa2 has already looked at every ASV before taxonomy is assigned. It is the region extractor (rule target_extract), and after cutting out the rRNA it aligns each ASV against its own reference set and sorts it into one origin: bacteria, archaea, eukaryota, chloroplast, mitochondria or uncertain. With organelles: metaxa2, the default, the filter also removes every ASV that Metaxa2 called mitochondria or chloroplast.

This is for organelle 16S that no token can reach. A plant mitochondrion whose classifier best hit is a bacterium is reported as a bacterium, so neither f__Mitochondria nor the best-hit check has anything to match.

How much is left for the organelle filter depends on the classifier and the reference. On the 16S test set (PRJNA305879) Metaxa2 calls 29 ASVs mitochondrial (28 in the SILVA 138.2 runs, whose ASV set differs slightly). With SILVA 144 the tokens and the best-hit check remove 26 of them under sintax but only 16 under rdp, which reports 9 of the other 13 as Enterobacterales. With SILVA 138.2 both methods remove 18 of the 28; of the other 10, rdp reports 8 as Enterobacterales, and sintax stops at phylum, class or order, mostly with a bacterial best hit below that rank. Metaxa2, which aligns each ASV against its own reference set, organelles included, calls such ASVs mitochondrial, so with the organelle filter on, the choice of classifier and release matters much less for which ASVs are kept.

The tokens stay useful next to it. On the 16S test set under sintax with SILVA 138.2, two ASVs that the classifier placed in Mitochondria (one in the reported lineage, one through the best-hit check) are called bacterial by Metaxa2; in the SILVA 144 runs, and under rdp with SILVA 138.2, there are none. The two signals overlap a lot but not completely, so the filter uses both.

What the filter takes from Metaxa2, and what it does not:

  • Only the organelle calls. Metaxa2's other calls (eukaryota, uncertain, the domains) remove nothing; which domains survive is still decided by keep.
  • Only Metaxa2's final answer, from its per-origin FASTA files under 05.dada2/metaxa2/, collected per ASV in 05.dada2/metaxa2_origin.tsv. Not the preliminary letter in the extraction headers, which calls far too many sequences mitochondrial (see 16S rRNA). That final call is stable from run to run, unlike Metaxa2's own taxonomy file, which the filter does not read.
  • It runs after keep, discard and the best-hit check, so it only removes what those three let through.

It can only act where Metaxa2 ran: 16S with extraction.enabled: true, and filter.enabled: true. For ITS, 18S, gyrB and rpoB, or with extraction off, the setting is inactive and the run says so once at start-up, instead of failing:

[MetaFlux] organelle filter: inactive — marker ITS does not run Metaxa2, so there is no organelle call to use

To switch it off, set organelles: off (null works too). The three filtered tables are then exactly what the tokens and the best-hit check alone give. Any other value stops the run at start-up.

The log lists what Metaxa2 found, how much of it the earlier steps had already removed, and every ASV that only Metaxa2 caught (16S test set, PRJNA305879, method: sintax, SILVA 144):

[assign_taxonomy/sintax] Organelle filter (Metaxa2 origin): 29 ASV(s), 2984 reads, called mitochondria (29) or chloroplast (0)
[assign_taxonomy/sintax]   already removed above by the tokens or the best-hit check: 26 ASV(s), 2977 reads (keep 0, discard 20, best-hit check 6)
[assign_taxonomy/sintax]   removed only by the organelle filter: 3 ASV(s), 7 reads
[assign_taxonomy/sintax]     ASV_199: mitochondria by Metaxa2, 3 reads (reported as d__Bacteria;k__Pseudomonadati;p__Pseudomonadota;c__Alphaproteobacteria;o__Hyphomicrobiales--other)
[assign_taxonomy/sintax]     ASV_219: mitochondria by Metaxa2, 2 reads (reported as d__Bacteria;k__Pseudomonadati;p__Pseudomonadota)
[assign_taxonomy/sintax]     ASV_226: mitochondria by Metaxa2, 2 reads (reported as d__Bacteria;k__Pseudomonadati;p__Pseudomonadota)

docs.title: The table with everything: asv_table_unfiltered.txt
docs.text:
Removed ASVs are not lost. Every run writes 06.taxonomy/asv_table_unfiltered.txt: the same layout as asv_table.txt, for every ASV that reached the filter, with two more columns.

Column Values metaxa2_origin Metaxa2's call: mitochondria, chloroplast, bacteria, archaea, eukaryota, uncertain. NA where Metaxa2 did not run (other markers, or extraction off) or made no call. Filled whenever Metaxa2 ran, also with organelles: off. filter_status kept, removed_keep, removed_discard, removed_best_hit or removed_organelle

An ASV that more than one step would remove is labelled with the first one, in the order the filter runs them: keep, discard, best-hit check, organelle filter. So removed_organelle means that only Metaxa2 caught it, while metaxa2_origin shows Metaxa2's opinion on every row, whatever the status. The kept rows are asv_table.txt exactly, and the read counts of all rows add up to the post_length_filter column of stats/read_tracking.txt. The tree and the other tables are built from the kept rows only.

This is the table for questions about the removed ASVs themselves — for example, which primer pair amplifies fewer organelles. The organelle share of each sample, in R:

tab    <- read.table("06.taxonomy/asv_table_unfiltered.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", row.names = 1)
counts <- tab[, !(names(tab) %in% c("taxonomy", "metaxa2_origin", "filter_status"))]
colSums(counts[tab$metaxa2_origin %in% c("mitochondria", "chloroplast"), ]) / colSums(counts)

This counts what Metaxa2 calls an organelle. To count what the tokens removed as well, add | tab$filter_status %in% c("removed_discard", "removed_best_hit") to the row selection — as long as discard lists only organelle tokens.

docs.title: Recommended starting points per marker
docs.text:
These are starting points, not defaults — nothing in the code applies them.

Marker keep discard 16S [d__Bacteria, d__Archaea] [o__Chloroplast, f__Mitochondria] ITS [k__Fungi] [] 18S [d__Eukaryota] — note this also drops PR2's organelle-tagged domains (d__Eukaryota:plas, :mito, :nucl, :apic, :chro) and the few ASVs left unclassified at Domain; see 18S rRNA [] gyrB no recommended default — see below rpoB no recommended default — see below

16S and 18S start with the domain, written d__ under both methods; ITS starts with the kingdom, k__, because UNITE has no domain rank. For 18S the taxonomy reference is PR2: SILVA-Eukaryotic only sizes the amplicon (the length probe) and never names an ASV, so its rank labels play no part in the filter.

gyrB has no recommended keep/discard, but it does have a filter worth applying, of a different kind. The DD7RZ8 reference tags every entry's first rank as gyrB (the true gene) or other (a co-amplified paralog such as parE). The tag is stored as an ordinary taxonomy rank, so a discard token removes the paralogs as it would any other taxon:

discard: [other]     # drops paralogs, keeps ASVs the classifier left unassigned

keep: [gyrB] is stricter, not equivalent — it also drops every ASV that came back unclassified, since an empty lineage matches no keep token.

Note the tag has no rank prefix — it is emitted verbatim as other or gyrB. How much other to expect depends on the primers and the samples, so a sensible first run leaves the lists empty, looks at the paralog fraction in the output, and decides after. See gyrB.

rpoB has nothing structurally equivalent. The FROGS RefSeq reference contains only rpoB, so there is no paralog or organellar class to filter at this stage. Leave the lists empty unless a particular run shows a reason not to. See rpoB.

docs.title: Writing tokens that actually match
docs.text:
Tokens are compared literally, so they have to be spelled exactly as the reference database spells them. The reliable way to get that right is to copy the name from the taxonomy column of 06.taxonomy/asv_table_unfiltered.txt, which lists every ASV of a run, the removed ones included.

The rank prefixes, and the markers whose strings have each rank:

Rank Prefix Markers Domain d__ 16S, 18S, rpoB Kingdom k__ 16S on SILVA 144, ITS Phylum p__ 16S, ITS, gyrB, rpoB Class c__ all five Order o__ all five Family f__ all five Genus g__ all five Species s__ all five; on 16S under rdp only

gyrB's first slot is its gene tag, gyrB or other, with no prefix. 18S has PR2's own ranks between the domain and the class: Supergroup sg__, Division dv__, Subdivision sbd__. The sintax path for 18S merges Division and Subdivision into a single dv__ field, so a subdivision-level token only exists on the rdp path.

Species-level tokens need extra care, because the exact form follows the reference and not the pipeline: SILVA (16S) via rdp yields a binomial with a space, e.g. s__Bacillus subtilis, while UNITE (ITS, under both methods), PR2 (18S), the GTDB-derived gyrB reference and the NCBI RefSeq-derived rpoB reference use an underscore, e.g. s__Staphylococcus_simiae. Copy, do not retype.

Tip

To drop lab or kit contaminants that a negative control revealed, add them to discard at the rank that identifies them cleanly — usually genus:

discard: [o__Chloroplast, f__Mitochondria, g__Ralstonia, g__Bradyrhizobium]

docs.title: When MetaFlux refuses a token at start-up
docs.text:
A token that no taxonomy string of the run can contain would remove every ASV in keep, or nothing in discard, and the run would only find out after the denoising and the classification. So the tokens are checked when the workflow is read, before any step runs, against the slots of the strings this run writes: the marker's ranks, for the taxonomy method and, for 16S, the SILVA release in use. One stop lists every problem and, where there is one, the token to write instead. The check runs also with enabled: false, so a wrong token is caught when it is written, not on the run that switches the filter on.

A token stops the run when:

Problem Examples its prefix is one this run's strings never have k__… on 16S with SILVA 138.2, or on rpoB; d__… on ITS; sbd__… on 18S under sintax; s__… on 16S under sintax it has no prefix (gyrB's gene tag excepted), or no name after the prefix Bacteria, d__ it puts a domain under k__, also where the strings have a k__ slot k__Bacteria, which stops with "write d__Bacteria" its name can never stand in that slot of the marker's reference d__Fungi on 16S; k__Fungi or k__Bacteroidota on 16S with SILVA 144; sg__Eukaryota on 18S; Other on gyrB; d__Archaea on rpoB it is not text: YAML reads a bare yes, no, null or a number as something else keep: [yes]

The last-but-one row uses the marker pack's reference_values, the rules the reference file itself has to pass before any classification (see the reference check). A trailing --other is dropped from a name before the check, as the filter itself drops it. The rules cover the top ranks only, and an ends_with rule checks only the ending: on SILVA 144 any name ending in ati passes as a kingdom, a misspelt k__Bacilati included.

A typical stop, for a 16S config written for MetaFlux v2.4.0 or earlier:

[MetaFlux] these amplicon.taxonomy.filter tokens can never match a taxonomy string of this run (16S, method sintax, release 144), so the run stops before any step:
  - amplicon.taxonomy.filter.keep: 'k__Bacteria' puts a domain under k__, which holds kingdoms in this table. Bacteria is a domain: write d__Bacteria.
  - amplicon.taxonomy.filter.keep: 'k__Archaea' puts a domain under k__, which holds kingdoms in this table. Archaea is a domain: write d__Archaea.
A token must equal one whole slot of the taxonomy string, prefix included. Since v2.5.0 the domain is always written d__, and k__ is the kingdom where the reference has one.

Where a prefix belongs to the marker but not to this run's taxonomy method, the message says why: an s__ token on 16S under sintax gets "16S under method: sintax writes no species", an sbd__ token on 18S under sintax "Under method sintax it is part of Division_Subdivision, written dv__".

What the check cannot see, because the names themselves are not checked there:

  • a misspelt name in a slot without a rule — a genus, a family, a species — passes and then matches nothing;
  • a 16S species written with an underscore: 16S writes s__Escherichia coli, with a space, so s__Escherichia_coli passes under rdp and matches nothing;
  • on 18S, a dv__ name in the other method's form: under sintax PR2 joins Division and Subdivision with "-" (dv__Opisthokonta-Fungi), so dv__Opisthokonta matches nothing there, and under rdp the joined form matches nothing (see 18S rRNA).

docs.title: When the filter empties the table
docs.text:
If the filter removes 100% of ASVs, the run stops with an error instead of writing a header-only table. Tokens that can never match stop the run at start-up already (above), so at this point the tokens fit the marker's strings but not the run: a token the marker has but the study does not want (an 18S d__Eukaryota left in a 16S config, where SILVA holds a few eukaryote records), a misspelt genus or family, or a taxon the samples simply do not hold. A silent empty table would be discovered much later, in R, with no clue as to why.

The error names the marker and the number of ASVs lost (numbers below are illustrative):

the keep/discard filter removed ALL 1843 ASVs (amp_type=ITS). The keep/discard lists likely do not match this marker: for 16S use keep: [d__Bacteria, d__Archaea]; for 18S keep: [d__Eukaryota]; for ITS keep: [k__Fungi]. Fix amplicon.taxonomy.filter, or set amplicon.taxonomy.filter.enabled: false.

If the organelle filter removed some of them, the message ends with how many, and that organelles: off keeps those: a 16S library that is nearly all organelle 16S (leaf or root tissue, say) can empty the table with perfectly good lists.

The check only fires when the filter is enabled and there were ASVs to begin with, so a run that produced no ASVs at all fails earlier and for its own reasons.

What to check, in order:

  1. The marker itself — is amplicon.type what the tokens were written for?
  2. The spelling, against the taxonomy column of a run made with enabled: false.
  3. Whether the samples hold the taxon at all, in 06.taxonomy/asv_table_unfiltered.txt of that run.

Run-to-run reproducibility of the filtered set

With a fixed amplicon.seed, the confidence values the filter reads come out the same at any thread count (sintax from v2.5.0 on), and so does the filtered ASV set. With rdp, DADA2's random tie-breaking can still move a bootstrap value between identical runs, and now and then flip an ASV's whole lineage, so that a token keeps or removes that ASV from one run to the next (see Troubleshooting).

docs.title: Seeing what the filter did
docs.text:
Both classifier paths log their counts to logs/assign_taxonomy.log, one line per step, saying how many ASVs each step cost (numbers illustrative):

[assign_taxonomy] Keep filter (d__Bacteria,d__Archaea): 1620 / 1843 ASVs retained
[assign_taxonomy] Discard filter (o__Chloroplast,f__Mitochondria): 47 ASV(s) removed
[assign_taxonomy] Discard filter, best-hit check (support >= 50%): 3 more ASV(s) removed
[assign_taxonomy] Organelle filter (Metaxa2 origin): 61 ASV(s), 8210 reads, called mitochondria (40) or chloroplast (21)
[assign_taxonomy]   already removed above by the tokens or the best-hit check: 48 ASV(s), 7930 reads (keep 0, discard 45, best-hit check 3)
[assign_taxonomy]   removed only by the organelle filter: 13 ASV(s), 280 reads
[assign_taxonomy] Final ASV count: 1557

The organelle lines appear on 16S runs only (followed by one line per ASV that only Metaxa2 caught, see above), and 06.taxonomy/asv_table_unfiltered.txt has the same information per ASV, in its filter_status column. The sintax path writes the same lines under an [assign_taxonomy/sintax] tag, except that it gives a best hit's support as a SINTAX confidence (best hit f__Mitochondria at 0.68 confidence) and the threshold as support >= 50.0%. A keep line that retains far fewer ASVs than expected is worth following up before trusting the table: often the reference simply failed to classify those ASVs at the rank the token names, rather than the ASVs being genuinely off-target.

Retired configuration keys

Earlier versions used regular expressions, include_pattern and exclude_pattern, which carried per-marker defaults. Those keys are gone. A config that still contains either of them stops the run at start-up with a message showing the keep/discard equivalent, rather than running with the filter silently disabled.

docs.title: The shotgun counterpart
docs.text:
Shotgun runs have their own filter, shotgun.taxonomy_filter, with three of the same keys (enabled, keep, discard; there is no best-hit check and no organelle filter) and exactly the same whole-segment token matching: keep first, then discard, and an empty list does nothing. It is applied to the final OTU table after Bracken, so it changes which OTUs appear in 03.abundance/otu_table.tsv and otu_table.biom, never how reads were classified.

One difference from the amplicon side: it ships off (enabled: false). Metagenomic sample types vary too much for a universal starting point; common uses are keep: [d__Bacteria, d__Archaea] for prokaryotes only, or discard: [g__Homo] as an explicit host safety net.

The OTU table always has eight slots, d__ k__ p__ c__ o__ f__ g__ s__, on any Kraken2 database. A virus has no domain: its d__ slot holds its realm (d__Duplodnaviria) or stays empty, so keep: [d__Bacteria, d__Archaea] also drops every virus, and so does [d__Bacteria, d__Archaea, d__Eukaryota], together with anything else without a domain (plasmids). To keep viruses, list their realms. A virus that NCBI places in no realm has an empty d__, so no realm token matches it: a keep list of realms drops it, and a discard list of realms leaves it in. Name it by a lower rank it does have: its family where there is one, otherwise its genus or species. Realm names follow the NCBI taxonomy the database was built with (the realm called Monodnaviria in older builds is Floreoviria in newer ones).

When Kraken2 runs, these tokens are checked at start-up as well, against the eight slots and against the database itself, whose domains, kingdoms and realms MetaFlux reads from its taxo.k2d file:

  • the run stops on a token with a wrong or missing prefix, a domain under k__ (k__Bacteria), Viruses under any prefix (no slot holds it; the message lists the database's realms instead), a realm under k__ (k__Duplodnaviria, write d__Duplodnaviria) and, with the filter on, a keep list none of whose tokens can match a row of this database;
  • it only warns about a well-formed token that this database gives no row: any k__ token on a GTDB database, which has no kingdom rank, or a domain, realm or kingdom the database does not have. One config can serve several databases, so this alone does not stop the run.

With profiler: sylph the tokens are not checked, because the filter acts on otu_table.tsv only and sylph's tables are written unfiltered.

Like the amplicon filter, it stops the run when it removes every OTU, instead of writing an empty table. The error names the tokens and lists the d__ values the table holds, which is usually enough to spot a token that does not fit the table. A table that is empty before the filter (no taxon at tax_lev in any sample) is still written, with a warning in the log.

See the shotgun overview and the configuration reference.

docs.title: Amplicon markers
docs.text:
MetaFlux runs one marker per amplicon run, chosen with amplicon.type in the config: 16S, ITS, 18S, gyrB or rpoB. Everything that differs between markers — which reference the amplicon-length probe measures, which database the classifier uses, whether a target-region extractor exists, how many taxonomic ranks the output carries — is declared in a small YAML file called a marker pack, one per marker, under workflow/markers/. The rest of the amplicon pipeline is the same code for all five.

Marker packs hold facts about the marker, never run settings. Primers, expected lengths, truncation values and taxon filters live in the run config; they are the things that change from one experiment to the next. A pack is read separately and is never merged into config, so no key is defined in both.

Note

A pack in config/markers/ shadows a shipped pack of the same name. Adding a marker is therefore a data-only change — a new pack file, no code edit — as long as its databases are plain downloads: the fetch rule is generated from the url the pack gives each reference. A database that arrives as an archive, or whose headers have to be reshaped before a classifier will read them, still needs a rule of its own in workflow/rules/amplicon/10_refdb.smk. That is how UNITE, the UNITE UCHIME subregions, the SILVA 144 training set (whose kingdom names lose SILVA's --other suffix), the SILVA SINTAX builds, the 18S PR2 SINTAX file (whose domain moves to the letter d:) and the FROGS rpoB build are handled.

A pack in config/markers/ replaces the shipped pack completely, so after an upgrade copy the shipped pack again and re-apply your change: every pack must declare reference_values (see the reference check), and a copy made for an older MetaFlux, which has none, stops the run at start-up, whichever marker the run uses.

docs.title: The five markers side by side
docs.text:
Marker What it is, what it resolves probe_mode Why that mode Taxonomy reference SINTAX build? Extractor Ranks 16S Bacterial/archaeal SSU rRNA; the standard prokaryote survey marker, genus-level for most taxa pcr SILVA ships full-length SSU genes, so the amplicon window has to be cut out with the primers SILVA 144 toGenus trainset, all seven SILVA ranks with the kingdom names written without --other (silva_train, built from silva_train_raw; SILVA 138.2 selectable), plus SILVA species assignment (silva_species) for DADA2 addSpecies Yes — silva_sintax, derived from the trainset by convert_silva_sintax. rdp and sintax both available Metaxa2 8 on SILVA 144 (Domain, Kingdom … Species), 7 on SILVA 138.2 ITS Fungal internal transcribed spacer, ITS1 or ITS2 (amplicon.its_region); the fungal barcode, species-level for well-represented lineages direct The UNITE UCHIME release is already the ITS1/ITS2 subregion plus a 15 bp anchor of flanking rRNA at each end, so lengths are read straight off it UNITE general release sh_general_release_dynamic_s_all_19.02.2025 (unite_fasta) Yes — UNITE UTAX release (unite_sintax). rdp and sintax both available ITSx 7 18S Eukaryotic SSU rRNA; protists and other micro-eukaryotes pcr The probe substrate (SILVA-Euk v132) is full-length SSU PR2 v5.1.1 SSU DADA2 file (pr2_dada2) Yes — pr2_sintax, PR2 v5.1.1's UTAX file (pr2_utax) with its domain moved to the SINTAX letter d:, built by convert_pr2_sintax. rdp and sintax both available none 9 under rdp, 8 under sintax gyrB DNA gyrase subunit B; protein-coding, single-copy, higher intra-genus resolution than 16S direct The DD7RZ8 v6 trainset is already primer-trimmed in-silico amplicons (~247 bp), not whole genes DD7RZ8 v6 trainset, GTDB r226 (gyrb_dada2) — the same file is the probe substrate No. rdp only none 7 (first rank is a paralog tag, not a taxon) rpoB RNA polymerase subunit B; protein-coding, single-copy in almost all bacteria, and assigns far more ASVs to species than a 16S V3–V4 amplicon does. Not a strain marker — the reference stops at species, so the output does too pcr The FROGS RefSeq build ships full-length rpoB genes (~4 kb), so in-silico PCR recovers the amplicon window, ~387 bp once the two primers are trimmed off (~435 bp including them) FROGS RefSeq rpoB build 20240707, converted to a DADA2 trainset (rpob_frogs) — the same file is the probe substrate No. rdp only none 7

Names in backticks are the pack's internal reference symbols. They belong to the workflow/markers/*.yaml packs, which use them to name the probe substrate (probe_ref) and the taxonomy databases (taxonomy_refdb, taxonomy_species_db, taxonomy_sintax_db); the workflow turns each symbol into a path at start-up. They are not run-config keys. Relocating a database in the run config uses a separate two-level key under references: — one level for the database family, one for the file — as in the config template:

references:
  silva:
    species: /shared/dbs/silva_v144_assignSpecies.fa.gz

A top-level silva_train: instead does nothing: the entry is ignored and the pack default is used. The key that relocates each symbol is in the table below.

docs.title: Which files get downloaded, and where
docs.text:
Each pack carries the download URL and the default on-disk location of every database it owns. Paths below are relative to references.refdb_root (default refdb). Files marked converted or extracted are not stored in the form they were downloaded in.

Marker Symbol File under refdb/ Role Run-config key that relocates it 16S silva_train_raw silva/silva_nr99_v144_toGenus_trainset.fa.gz probe substrate; SILVA 144 training set as published (seven ranks) silva.train_raw 16S silva_train silva/silva_nr99_v144_toGenus_7rank_other-verbatim_trainset.fa.gz rdp trainset — converted from silva_train_raw (the same seven ranks, kingdom names without --other) silva.train 16S silva_species silva/silva_v144_assignSpecies.fa.gz DADA2 addSpecies (16S only) silva.species 16S silva_sintax silva/silva_nr99_v144_7rank_other-verbatim_sintax.fa.gz sintax database — converted from silva_train silva.sintax ITS unite_fasta unite/sh_general_release_dynamic_s_all_19.02.2025.fasta rdp trainset — extracted from a .tgz unite.fasta ITS unite_sintax unite/utax_reference_dataset_all_19.02.2025.fasta.gz sintax database unite.sintax ITS unite_uchime_ITS1 unite/uchime_its1.fasta probe substrate when its_region: ITS1 — extracted from a .zip unite.uchime_its1 ITS unite_uchime_ITS2 unite/uchime_its2.fasta probe substrate when its_region: ITS2 — extracted from a .zip unite.uchime_its2 18S silva_euk silva_euk/silva_132.18s.dada2.fa.gz probe substrate only silva_euk.fasta 18S pr2_dada2 pr2/pr2_SSU_dada2.fasta.gz rdp trainset pr2.dada2 18S pr2_utax pr2/pr2_SSU_UTAX.fasta.gz PR2's UTAX file as published; the input of pr2_sintax pr2.utax 18S pr2_sintax pr2/pr2_SSU_UTAX_domain-first.fasta.gz sintax database — converted from pr2_utax (the domain moved to the letter d:) pr2.sintax gyrB gyrb_dada2 gyrb/train_set_gyrB_v6.fa.gz probe substrate + rdp trainset gyrb.dada2 rpoB rpob_frogs rpob/rpob_refseq_cc_20240707_domain-d_dada2.fa.gz probe substrate + rdp trainset — converted from the FROGS archive (the domain written d__) rpob.frogs

The 16S rows are those of the default release, SILVA 144; other-verbatim becomes other-stripped with amplicon.taxonomy.silva_other: strip. With references.silva.release: "138.2" the 16S files are silva/silva_nr99_v138.2_toGenus_trainset.fa.gz, silva/silva_v138.2_assignSpecies.fa.gz and silva/silva_nr99_v138.2_sintax.fa.gz, and there is no silva_train_raw. See 16S rRNA. A converted file is written where its run-config key points, and rebuilt there when its input or its conversion script is newer (see reference files MetaFlux builds itself).

Everything here is fetched on first use and cached, so a second run reuses it. Apart from references.silva.release, which picks the SILVA release for 16S, the only reason to put a references: entry in the run config is to point MetaFlux at a copy that already exists somewhere else, for example a shared directory on a cluster.

docs.title: What probe_mode means
docs.text:
Before DADA2 runs, MetaFlux measures how long the amplicon is expected to be, and uses that distribution to size the truncation lengths and the ASV length filter. That measurement is the amplicon-length probe (rule amplicon_probe), and it only runs when amplicon.expected_length is set to auto. probe_mode decides how the measurement is taken.

pcr — in-silico PCR. The probe takes the supplied primer FASTAs and runs two cutadapt passes against a full-length reference: first keep the reference sequences in which the forward primer matches, trimming it and everything upstream, then, of those, keep the ones in which the reverse-complemented reverse primer matches, trimming it and everything downstream. Neither match is anchored — the references are whole genes, so the primers bind inside them. What survives is the set of amplicons those primers would produce from that reference, and their lengths are the distribution. This is the mode for 16S, 18S and rpoB, because SILVA, SILVA-Euk and the FROGS rpoB build all contain whole genes. For rpoB a third pass leaves out of the statistics the products that still hold a second forward-primer site (see A primer that matches twice).

direct — no PCR simulation at all. The reference is already amplicon-length, so cutadapt is never called and the sequence lengths are read off the file as they are. This is the mode for ITS, whose UNITE UCHIME reference is the pre-extracted ITS1 or ITS2 subregion, and for gyrB, whose DD7RZ8 trainset was itself built by cutting in-silico amplicons with the Barret 2015 primers.

With the wrong mode, in-silico PCR against a pre-trimmed reference finds no primer binding sites left to cut against, so it recovers nothing. For ITS this follows from where the primers bind: ITS1F and ITS4 sit in the flanking rRNA genes, and those binding sites are not part of a UNITE sequence (the UCHIME references keep only a 15 bp anchor of flanking rRNA at each end).

Both modes end at the same place: one JSON of length statistics (n_amplicons, min, q1, median, q3, p95, p99, max, mean, stdev, plus excluded_taxa and n_excluded, and for rpoB n_excluded_second_site) cached in the pipeline's own refdb/cache/, next to the workflow. That directory is fixed at the repository root and does not follow references.refdb_root, so the cache stays put across runs and output directories even when the databases themselves live on a shared path. The file is keyed by marker, reference tag (for 16S including the lineages left out of the statistics, for rpoB the third pass) and a hash of the two primer sequences. Change a primer and the probe re-runs; leave it alone and it is reused. Which single statistic becomes expected_length comes from amplicon.probe_length_stat — see amplicon length and truncation.

Note

probe_mode is set in the marker pack, not in the run config. It is checked at start-up: anything other than pcr or direct stops the run with has an invalid probe_mode … must be 'pcr' or 'direct'.

docs.title: What "no extractor" means
docs.text:
For 16S and ITS, MetaFlux can isolate the target region within each ASV before taxonomy is assigned — Metaxa2 for 16S, ITSx for ITS. This is the target_extract rule, switched on with amplicon.extraction.enabled.

18S, gyrB and rpoB have extractor: none. There is no equivalent tool for gyrB or rpoB, and for 18S the pack deliberately does not use Metaxa2 even though it could handle SSU. Those markers define no target_extract rule at all, so if the config still asks for extraction the workflow would otherwise go looking for a file nothing produces. Instead the setting is overridden at start-up and the reason is printed:

[MetaFlux] warning: marker 18S has no target-region extractor; ignoring amplicon.extraction.enabled: true (no extraction step will run)

Nothing else changes. The ASV length filter still runs, and it is what keeps ASVs inside the window derived from the probe distribution. Setting extraction.enabled: false explicitly for these three markers has exactly the same effect and avoids the warning.

docs.title: Taxonomy methods per marker
docs.text:
amplicon.taxonomy.method chooses between rdp (DADA2's naive Bayesian classifier, with min_boot as the bootstrap cutoff) and sintax (VSEARCH, with sintax_cutoff). A marker can only offer sintax if a SINTAX-formatted build of its reference exists. For gyrB and rpoB none does — DD7RZ8 and the FROGS release both ship a DADA2 trainset only — so the pack leaves taxonomy_sintax_db empty and the run stops at start-up rather than failing somewhere deep in the taxonomy rule:

[MetaFlux] marker gyrB has no SINTAX reference database, so amplicon.taxonomy.method: sintax is not available for it. Use method: rdp.

DADA2's addSpecies step, which adds a species call on top of the genus-level assignment, applies to 16S only — it is the one marker whose pack names a taxonomy_species_db. The other four have no second species step because their single reference already carries a species rank: PR2 for 18S, DD7RZ8 for gyrB, the converted FROGS build for rpoB, and UNITE's native s__Genus_species for ITS.

docs.title: Rank models
docs.text:
Each pack declares the rank columns its classifier emits and the prefixes used to render them (d__, k__, p__, …). The ranks are those of the marker's reference, nothing added and nothing removed: d__ is always the domain slot and k__ always the kingdom slot, and a table has a kingdom only where its reference defines one. So the markers differ:

Marker Ranks 16S, SILVA 144 Domain, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species 16S, SILVA 138.2 Domain, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species ITS Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species (UNITE has no domain) 18S, rdp Domain, Supergroup, Division, Subdivision, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species 18S, sintax Domain, Supergroup, Division_Subdivision, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species gyrB Gene (the paralog tag), Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species rpoB Domain, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species

The prefix of each rank, and the shotgun tables next to these, are in taxonomy strings in the final tables.

16S declares its ranks per SILVA release, because SILVA 144 added the kingdom that 138.2 does not have. 18S declares two models, one per taxonomy method: PR2's DADA2 file has Division and Subdivision, its UTAX file one field that joins the two. Prefixes are keyed to what a rank means rather than to the letter code in the reference, so a d__, sg__ or c__ … s__ token works under either method; a Division token does not (see 18S rRNA).

Two prefix styles exist. Under bare (16S, 18S) the reference values carry no prefix and the builder adds them. Under embedded (ITS, gyrB, rpoB) the values already arrive with their prefixes attached (k__Fungi in UNITE, d__Bacteria in the converted FROGS file) and are emitted verbatim. Either way the taxonomy strings in the final table look the same, which is what the keep/discard filter matches against — see keeping and discarding taxa.

In gyrB the first rank is not a taxon: DD7RZ8 tags every reference as gyrB (the real gene) or other (a co-amplified paralog such as parE). Keeping that tag as rank 1 means paralogs can be dropped with the ordinary taxon filter (discard: [other]) instead of a mechanism of their own.

docs.title: The reference check (reference_values)
docs.text:
Before any ASV is classified, rule check_taxonomy_reference reads the exact file the classifier is about to use, a path pinned in the run config included, and checks every header against the pack:

  • the rank shape: in a DADA2 training set (rdp) no lineage may be deeper than the pack's ranks (for 16S without the species, which addSpecies fills from a file of its own), and the deepest lineages must reach them; a shallower lineage must end with ;, as SILVA's do, so that assignTaxonomy pads it with empty ranks; the names carry the pack's prefixes where the reference embeds them; a SINTAX file must use the pack's letters, in the pack's top-down order;
  • the names in the ranks the pack has rules for, its reference_values.

A file that fails stops the run before any classification. The message names the file, the rank, the wrong names with their counts, and example headers. The usual causes are a run config that pins a wrong file (another SILVA release's, say) or a reference that changed upstream; the fix is the right file, or a new release block in the pack. When the file passes, the check writes stats/taxonomy_reference_check.json, a record of what it saw, and the taxonomy step can start. The check takes seconds, and it starts as soon as its reference is there, long before the denoising ends.

A rule names a rank of the pack and lists, per kind, the names allowed there:

  • one_of: the names allowed in this rank;
  • ends_with: allowed endings (a name passes when it is in one_of or ends with one of these);
  • not_one_of: names that must never appear in this rank.

The shipped packs declare:

Marker reference_values 16S, both releases Domain: one_of [Bacteria, Archaea, Eukaryota] 16S, SILVA 144 Kingdom: ends_with [ati], one_of [Incertae Sedis] ITS Kingdom: not_one_of [Bacteria, Archaea, Eukaryota] 18S Domain: one_of PR2's eight domain values (Eukaryota, Bacteria, Archaea and the organelle tags Eukaryota:plas, :mito, :nucl, :apic, :chro); Supergroup: not_one_of the same eight gyrB Gene: one_of [gyrB, other] rpoB Domain: one_of [Bacteria]

With the rank shape, these rules catch a reference whose ranks have shifted: SILVA's own 144 download, whose kingdoms carry --other; a SILVA 138.2 file used as 144, with its phyla where the kingdoms should be; PR2's own UTAX file, which holds the domain under the letter k: and the supergroup under d:; the rpoB file of an earlier MetaFlux, which wrote the domain as k__. The same rules check the keep/discard tokens when the run starts (see when MetaFlux refuses a token at start-up).

When you write a pack of your own:

  • Every pack declares reference_values, at its top level or in every release block. A pack without it stops the run at start-up, whichever marker the run uses. A pack for a marker of your own may write reference_values: {} to have the rank shape checked and no names.
  • A rule applies only where its rank exists. For 18S, a rule for Division (or Subdivision) is tested under method: rdp, which reads the DADA2 file, and left out under sintax, with one line at start-up saying so; a rule for Division_Subdivision works the other way round. A rank that is in neither rank model stops the run.
  • A 16S rule for Species stops the run at start-up: addSpecies fills that rank from a file of its own, after the classification, so neither file the check reads has a species to test.
  • A mistake in a rule (a misspelt rank or kind, an empty list, a name YAML does not read as text) stops the run at start-up too, under either method.

docs.text:
• 16S rRNA — bacteria and archaea, SILVA, Metaxa2 extraction, species assignment
  • ITS — fungi, UNITE, ITSx extraction, ITS1 vs ITS2
  • 18S rRNA — eukaryotes, probed on SILVA-Euk and classified on PR2, 9 ranks under rdp and 8 under sintax
